subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Morgan Price <morgan.price@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Dec 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs follow-up - quick clarification

Hey Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier — that was helpful. A couple quick clarifying items as we prepare our side for a short benchmark:

- Our main concern is end-to-end latency (client -> API -> model -> response) for our primary search/rewrite endpoint.
- Target production SLOs we want to qualify against are p95 <= 400ms and p99 <= 1.2s for typical 256-token generation (non-streaming). We also need streaming to start returning tokens within 150ms and keep tail latency reasonable.
- Concurrency: our peak concurrent request figure today is ~120 concurrent requests (we can provide trace samples). Typical sustained traffic is 40-60 rps, bursts up to 200 rps during market opens.

Can you confirm if those SLOs are where we should focus for the benchmark, and whether Redwood hosted can hit p95/p99 numbers significantly better than our current provider?

I'll attach a small trace sample from our QA environment in a follow-up email (sanitized).

Thanks,
Morgan
Director of Infrastructure
FinLytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Price <morgan.price@finlytics.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs follow-up - quick clarification

Hi Morgan — great to chat and thanks for the clear targets. Recapping below and proposing next steps so everyone is aligned.

Recap of your targets (as I heard them):
- Non-streaming end-to-end: p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 1.2s (256-token gen)
- Streaming: first-token within ~150ms; sustained stream token cadence such that user-perceived latency stays low
- Concurrency/throughput: sustained 40-60 rps, peak bursts up to ~200 rps; current peak concurrent requests ~= 120

Redwood hosted baseline (what we typically see for similar gen workloads):
- Non-streaming end-to-end (hosted API, default batching + prefix cache): p95 ~ 220-350ms, p99 ~ 450-900ms for 256-token generation depending on model variant and quantization.
- Streaming: first-byte ~80-140ms, with tail depending on model output length and client network.
- Concurrency: we support sustained ranges you mentioned; recommended reserved concurrency window for predictable p99 is to configure a dedicated pool (we can provision a short-term Dedicated-like pool for the benchmark).

Important notes / questions for the benchmark:
1) Baseline model: which model variant are you currently using with your provider (name + size + quantization)? That will affect comparability — please include in the trace sample.
2) Payloads: please send a sample of representative request payloads (we got the QA trace sample you mentioned — thanks).
3) Network topology: are you calling from US-West -> provider in US-West? Any VPC peering or egress constraints?
4) Streaming mode: do you use server-sent events (SSE) or chunked HTTP for streaming? We can reproduce both.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: share sanitized trace (payloads + timestamps) and indicate model variant + quantization.
- Us (Redwood): run a 2-hour benchmark during an agreed window using your trace (we'll run both hosted API and a Dedicated-like reserved pool config), produce p50/p95/p99 E2E numbers and per-token cost estimates, and share artifacts (traces, dashboards, and a short one-pager).
- Coordinate a 1-hour post-benchmark review call to go over results and recommended config for production.

Attachments I'm including: redwood_perf_onepager.pdf (short overview of what we measure) and redwood_benchmark_instructions.pdf (test plan & data format).

If that all looks good I can loop in Marissa (sales engineering) and Aditya (solutions eng) to schedule the benchmark and handle config details.

Best,
Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Price <morgan.price@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs follow-up - quick clarification

Laura — thanks for the quick recap. A few answers from our side so you can scope the benchmark:

- Model: currently on provider-X gpt-neoX-2.7B, running FP16; no quantization today.
- Network: client traffic originates from our US-East and US-West clusters (we can prefer US-West for the benchmark to match your hosted region).
- Streaming: we use chunked HTTP responses in our client implementation; SSE is not used.
- Baseline numbers (measured from our synthetic load): non-streaming p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 2.8s for a 256-token generation (this is including our network hops and provider latency). First token for streaming typically shows ~420ms on average.

We're comfortable proceeding with your suggested plan — please loop in engineering and propose two windows (one this week, one early next week) for the 2-hour run.

Thanks,
Raj
Engineering Manager, FinLytics

Laura
